In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

I said: 'I am not one who reads.' He pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of exhaustion, then he released me and said: 'Read!' I said: 'I am not one who reads.' He pressed me a third time until I reached the limit of exhaustion, then he released me and said: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾ until he reached ﴿what he did not know﴾." He said: So he returned with it, his shoulders trembling, until he entered upon Khadijah and said: "Cover me, cover me!" So they covered him until the fear had left him. Then he said: "O Khadijah, what is wrong with me?" He told her the news and said: "I have feared for myself." She said to him: "Never! Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. Indeed, you join the ties of kinship, speak the truth, bear the burdens of others, provide for the guest, and help in the misfortunes of truth." Then Khadijah set out with him until she brought him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy, who was the cousin of Khadijah, the brother of her father. He had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic era, and he used to write the Arabic script, and he wrote in Arabic from the Gospel what Allah willed that he write. He was an old man who had gone blind. Khadijah said: "O cousin, listen to your nephew." Waraqah said: "Nephew, what do you see?" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had seen. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will they expel me?" Waraqah said: "Yes. No man has ever come with what you have brought except that he was opposed. Whenever he reached the summit of a mountain to cast himself down from it, Jibril would appear to him and say: "O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of Allah." Thereby his heart would be calmed and his soul would be at rest, and he would return. When the pause in revelation lengthened upon him, he would go out for the same purpose, and when he reached the summit of the mountain, Jibril would appear to him and say to him the same thing.

This is the quality by which Adam, the father of mankind, was distinguished over the angels. Knowledge is sometimes in the minds, sometimes in the tongue, and sometimes in writing by the fingers: mental, verbal and written. Written knowledge necessitates the other two, but not conversely. Therefore He said: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾. In the report it is said: "Bind knowledge with writing." [This is reported from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) as a mawquf report, narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/106), Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (9/49), and al-Darimi in al-Sunan, no. (503). From Anas as a mawquf report, narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/106) and al-Ramahurmuzi in al-Muhaddith al-Fasil (p. 368).
